positioning: Kubernetes v1.37 focuses on API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, Dynamic Resource Allocation, and CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies. For operators, this release translates 396 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Dynamic Resource Allocation
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.

high_level_changes.headline: CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.

high_level_changes.headline: Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.

high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.

jargon_glossary.meaning: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Built-in kubelet provisioning and rotation of X.509 mTLS identity certificates directly into Pods without third-party sidecars.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Simplifies zero-trust pod-to-pod mTLS without managing complex external webhook/cert-manager plumbing.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Concise Binary Object Representation (RFC 8949) as a compact binary alternative to JSON for Kubernetes API client-server serialization.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Reduces API server CPU spent on JSON parsing and lowers network bandwidth for custom resources (CRDs) that couldn't use Protobuf.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

should_i_upgrade.text: ACTION REQUIRED: Graduated the `SELinuxMount` feature gate to GA. The feature is enabled by default in `v1.37`, which may break existing workloads in clusters with SELinux enabled. Please see [the Kubernetes blog post](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2026/04/22/breaking-changes-in-selinux-volume-labeling/) to identify potentially problematic workloads in a `v1.36` cluster and how to fix them or opt out of `SELinuxMount` changes before upgrading to `v1.37`. Admins of clusters without SELinux enabled can ignore this release note. ([#139956](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139956), [@jsafrane](https://github.com/jsafrane)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps and Node]

ACTION REQUIRED: Converted the `DisruptionMode` enum field to a struct to support future extensibility. Promoted the `scheduling.k8s.io` API group from `v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3` and dropped `v1alpha2` entirely. Remove all `v1alpha2` objects from the `kube-apiserver` before performing the cluster update. ([#138572](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138572), [@dom4ha](https://github.com/dom4ha)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, CLI, Etcd, Node, Scheduling and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, CLI, Etcd, Node, Scheduling and Testing

should_i_upgrade.text: ACTION REQUIRED: Fixed `eventRecordQPS` handling in `kubelet` configuration to treat 0 as unlimited (no rate limit), aligning behavior with the documentation. Users relying on the previous default behavior should explicitly set a non-zero value (for example, 50). ([#117119](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117119), [@HirazawaUi](https://github.com/HirazawaUi)) [SIG API Machinery, Auth and Node]

ACTION REQUIRED: Updated the `kubelet` to log its effective configuration at startup. Because these logs can expose configuration details, cluster administrators should restrict the `nodes/logs` ClusterRole to trusted users. This is largely a reminder of an existing best practice, since most effective configuration values can already be inferred from other log messages or `kubelet` behavior. ([#139837](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139837), [@SergeyKanzhelev](https://github.com/SergeyKanzhelev)) [SIG Node]

Changed `kubeadm` to explicitly set `KubeProxyConfiguration.mode` to iptables when `KubeProxyConfiguration` is not provided or when the `mode` field is empty. In `v1.37`, `kube-proxy` will warn if the field is not explicitly set as part of the planned transition to nftables as the default mode in a future release. ([#139777](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139777), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123)) [SIG Cluster Lifecycle]
Deprecated the ignored `--filename`/`-f` flag on `kubectl run`. ([#138671](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138671), [@Suknna](https://github.com/Suknna)) [SIG CLI]

Locked the deprecated `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` feature gate to its default value; it can no longer be set. ([#139212](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139212), [@yongruilin](https://github.com/yongruilin)) [SIG API Machinery]

`kubeadm`: Added a (delayed) warning that `kube-proxy`'s ipvs mode is deprecated since `v1.35` and users on newer Linux kernels should be using the nftables mode instead, which became GA in `v1.33`. For older kernel versions, users can use iptables, which is still the default. ([#139067](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139067), [@neolit123](https://github.com/neolit123)) [SIG Cluster Lifecycle]

wheres_the_proof.text: Added Beta support for compressed responses to `WatchList` requests. When a client sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, the API server returns a gzip compressed response. This behavior is enabled by default and can be disabled using the `WatchListCompression` feature gate. Regular `watch` requests are unaffected. ([#140140](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140140), [@p0lyn0mial](https://github.com/p0lyn0mial)) [SIG API Machinery]

Added the `WatchListCompression` feature gate (Beta, enabled by default) to compress `WatchList` responses with gzip for clients that send `Accept-Encoding: gzip`. Regular `Watch` requests are unaffected. ([#139308](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139308), [@p0lyn0mial](https://github.com/p0lyn0mial)) [SIG API Machinery]

Updated admission webhooks to skip auth/authz virtual resources, such as `tokenreviews` and `subjectaccessreviews`, that ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicy already exclude. Added the `ExcludeAdmissionWebhookVirtualResources` feature gate in Beta, enabled by default, with an opt-out option to restore the previous behavior. ([#140019](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140019), [@BenTheElder](https://github.com/BenTheElder)) [SIG API Machinery and Testing]

Graduated Pod Certificates to GA, with the PodCertificateRequest feature gate enabled by default. The `PKIXPublicKey` and `ProofOfPossession` fields, deprecated in PodCertificateRequest `v1beta1`, are removed from the `v1` API. Update clients that still set these fields before upgrading. ([#139579](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139579), [@yt2985](https://github.com/yt2985)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Architecture, Auth, Etcd, Node, Scheduling and Testing]
sigs: API Machinery, Apps, Architecture, Auth, Etcd, Node, Scheduling and Testing

Please see [the Kubernetes blog post](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2026/04/22/breaking-changes-in-selinux-volume-labeling/) to identify potentially problematic workloads in a `v1.36` cluster and how to fix them or opt out of `SELinuxMount` changes before upgrading to `v1.37`. # What's New in Kubernetes v1.37

## High-Level Explanation
Kubernetes v1.37 focuses on API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, Dynamic Resource Allocation, and CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies. For operators, this release translates 396 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **Dynamic Resource Allocation**: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.
- **CEL-Based Validating & Mutating Admission Policies**: Improves cel-based validating & mutating admission policies for platform security guardrails, multi-tenant compliance policies, and default resource injectors running on in-process `kube-apiserver` admission chain (replaces external webhook deployments), delivering removes dedicated webhook pods and eliminates deployment outages caused by webhook timeouts.
- **Networking, `nftables` Proxy & Traffic Observability**: Improves networking, `nftables` proxy & traffic observability for high-throughput east-west microservices and latency-sensitive ingress traffic running on linux dataplane (`nftables`/`ipvs`) and cloud load balancers, delivering lowers cross-AZ data transfer costs (`trafficDistribution`) and reduces node CPU spent on iptables rules.
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Gang Scheduling (`Workload` / `PodGroup`)**: An 'all-or-nothing' scheduling guarantee where a group of cooperating Pods (like a multi-node training or distributed inference job) only starts when capacity exists for the entire group. Why it matters: Prevents expensive GPUs from sitting idle in deadlocked partial allocations when a cluster is near capacity.
- **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy & MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL)**: In-process policy rules written in Common Expression Language (CEL) evaluated directly inside `kube-apiserver` without calling external admission webhook servers. Why it matters: Removes webhook network latency and prevents a crashed policy pod from taking down cluster deployments.
- **WatchList & Snapshottable Watch Cache**: Streaming object lists from `kube-apiserver` memory cache snapshots instead of assembling giant one-shot payloads from `etcd`. Why it matters: Slashes API server RAM spikes and protects `etcd` from OOM crashes during controller restarts on large clusters.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **Pod Certificates (`PodCertificateRequest`)**: Built-in kubelet provisioning and rotation of X.509 mTLS identity certificates directly into Pods without third-party sidecars. Why it matters: Simplifies zero-trust pod-to-pod mTLS without managing complex external webhook/cert-manager plumbing.
- **HPA Scale-to-Zero (`minReplicas: 0`)**: Allows `HorizontalPodAutoscaler` to scale external/queue-driven workloads all the way down to 0 replicas when idle and wake them when queue depth rises. Why it matters: Directly cuts cloud compute and GPU bills for bursty batch/inference workers during off-peak hours.
- **CBOR Encoding for Kubernetes API**: Concise Binary Object Representation (RFC 8949) as a compact binary alternative to JSON for Kubernetes API client-server serialization. Why it matters: Reduces API server CPU spent on JSON parsing and lowers network bandwidth for custom resources (CRDs) that couldn't use Protobuf.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.
